spans.s:
āhnika
(‘that which is done in a day’)
------------------------------------------
According to the धर्मशास्त्रस्, every द्विज (‘the twice-born,’ i.e., the ब्राह्मण, the क्षत्त्रिय and the वैश्य) has to follow a strictly regulated daily routine. Every item of it, even those pertaining to the physical needs of the body, should be considered and performed as a religious duty. Such an attitude is conducive to his spiritual welfare.
Such duties as are to be performed during the course of an ‘ahan’ or day, are called ‘āhnika.’ Day-time, for practical purposes, was extended for a short time before sunrise and after sunset. This period was usually divided into eight equal parts and different items of the daily routine were assigned to different periods of the day.
Principal matters discussed under आह्निक are: बोधन and utthāna (getting up from the bed), शौच (bodily purity), दन्तधावन (brushing the teeth), स्नान (bath), सन्ध्या (prayers to be offered at dawn), जप (repetition of mantras), तर्पण (libations to forefathers), पञ्चमहायज्ञस् (five daily sacrifices), होम (attending to the sacrificial fire), देवपूजा (worship of God), भोजन (taking ड़ोओद्), arthasañcayana (earning wealth), स्वाध्याय and pravacana (studying and teaching the वेदस्), evening सन्ध्या, दान (giving gifts) and निद्रा (going to sleep).
Each one of these has been described in great detail in the smṛtis and digests often noting the alternatives or variations. The more important of these can be briefly described here.
Contemplating on God and holy beings is the first duty to be done, on waking up. Answering calls of nature should be done in consonance with the rules of health and sanitation. Bath should be taken in cold water, preferably in a river or a pond, repeating the Aghamarṣaṇa सूक्त, the Puruṣa sūkta and other prescribed Vedic hymns. A householder is expected to bathe twice a day, once before sunrise and again before noon. While bathing, तर्पण (offering water ceremonially to gods, sages and manes) should also be done. Along with wearing fresh washed clothes after bath, putting the tilaka or caste mark (ūrdhva-पुण्ड्र, तिर्यक्पुण्ड्र, चन्दन and so on) is also recommended. Then come the सन्ध्या ritual and गायत्री जप. This is followed by होम, offering libations of milk in the consecrated fire. Study of Vedic texts, feeding guests and animals, devoting time to the earning of wealth for maintain-ing the family are other items of daily routine.
For details, see under the respective title.
The word आह्निक has been used as the name of the various chapters or sections of the Mahābhāṣya (the great commentary) by पतञ्जलि on the grammatical sūtras of पाणिनि.
